課程綱要.課程名稱(英文): Introduction to the IPCC assessment reports
課程綱要.課程目標: 本課程旨在幫助學生深入理解並解讀《政府間氣候變化專門委員會（IPCC）》報告，掌握其核心內容和科學依據，並能夠將報告中的關鍵資訊應用於政策制定、社會行動及日常生活中。具體課程目標包括： 理解IPCC報告的結構與內容、掌握氣候變化的科學基礎、分析氣候變化的社會、了解減緩與適應策略、提升氣候行動的能力、促進批判性思維與討論、培養跨學科合作精神。本課程適合所有對氣候變化有興趣的學者、政策制定者、環保工作者及任何希望了解氣候變化科學和應對策略的社會大眾。
課程綱要.授課內容:
本課程前4週預計邀請相關專家做主題演講，接續2週老師導讀，其餘週次由6位老師帶領學生做不同主題之分組報告，每組報告2次。
第一週
主題：IPCC報告導論與課程概述
第二週
主題：氣候科學與氣候變遷
第三週
主題：氣候變遷衝擊與調適
第四週
主題：氣候變遷的國際合作

課程綱要.課程目標: 本課程介紹二氧化碳封存原理與選址準則、建立二氧化碳封存場之地下三維地質模型、灌注後二氧化碳團塊移棲模擬及風險分析，二氧化碳灌注井設計及後續監測、報告與驗證之準則，碳封存場營運期間之風險評估與管理。全週期計畫管理與經濟分析等。
課程綱要.授課內容:
模組 1 — 碳捕捉與封存（CCS）概論
主題內容
• 全球暖化背景與二氧化碳地質封存於減碳的角色
• CCS 價值鏈概述
• 法規架構與國際標準（如 ISO 27914）
• 封存場址類型：鹽水層、枯竭油氣田
________________________________________
模組 2 — 二氧化碳地質封存的地質基礎
主題內容
• 基礎地質：地層學、構造地質學、沉積學
• 儲集層特性
• 封蓋層特性
• 地質力學基礎
• 台灣地質與潛在碳封存場址
實作練習
• 岩心樣本解讀
• 岩石薄片鑑定
• 基本儲集層性質計算
________________________________________
模組 3 — 地下地質資料獲取與解析
主題內容
• 震測勘探方法（2D、3D、時移震測）
• 基本鑽井
• 井測與岩石物理
• 井下應力與流體測量
• 岩心實驗室分析
• 地球化學特徵（地層水、礦物組成）
操作實作
• 使用業界軟體 Petrel 進行震測剖面解釋
• 使用業界軟體 Techlog 進行井測資料分析
________________________________________
模組 4 — 場址篩選與選址
主題內容
• 潛在封存場址的選址準則
• 封存量估算方法
• 風險篩選與排序方法
• 利害關係人、土地使用與環境考量
實務活動
• 封存量計算工作坊
• 多個候選場址的篩選練習
________________________________________
模組 5 — 儲集層建模與模擬
主題內容
• 靜態地質模型建構（地質模型建立）
• 動態流體模擬：CO₂ 團塊移動、滯留機制
• 地質力學建模
• 聯合行為：水–力–化學耦合過程
• 不確定性量化
實作內容
• 建立基本靜態三維地質模型
• 執行 CO₂ 注入模擬
________________________________________
模組 6 — 二氧化碳注入井設計
主題內容
• 二氧化碳注入井設計
• 材料相容性（腐蝕、固井完整性）
• 井完井策略
• 注入操作參數
實習/工作坊
• 設計一套基本的 CO₂ 注入井完井方案
________________________________________
模組 7 — 監測、報告與驗證（MRV）
主題內容
• MRV在碳封存計畫的目的與重要性
• 監測井設計
• 地表/近地表監測（地氣、通量測量）
• 地層監測（陸域與海域）：震測、壓力、微震
• 儲集層上方監測
• 井筒完整性監測
• 衛星與遙測應用
• MRV法規與程序設計（ISO 27916）
實作
• 設計一個碳封存場址的 MRV 計畫
________________________________________
模組 8 — 風險評估與管理
主題內容
• 潛在洩漏途徑：井筒、斷層、裂隙、蓋層
• 危害識別（HAZID）
• 機率式風險評估
• 環境衝擊與緩解措施
• 誘發地震管理
練習
• 建立風險矩陣與緩解方案
________________________________________
模組 9 — 專案開發與經濟分析
主題內容
• 二氧化碳封存專案生命週期階段（篩選 → 操作 → 關閉）
• 成本模型（CAPEX、OPEX）
• 商業模式與融資選項
• 法規遵循與許可流程
• 社區參與與社會授權（social license）
工作坊
• 預算與時程估算
• 許可流程規劃
________________________________________
模組 10 — 操作、關閉與長期管理
主題內容
• 注入操作與效能追蹤
• 可調適儲集層管理
• 場址關閉標準
• 關閉後監測義務
• 移交主管機關與長期責任
________________________________________

學生需設計一套完整的 CO₂ 地質封存場址開發計畫，包括：
• 場址選擇

• 風險評估

課程綱要.課程目標: 本課程設計為提供學生對空氣污染監測技術與污染管制策略之系統性理解，內容涵蓋空氣污染物之量測原理、監測儀器、資料品質控管、污染來源解析，以及相關管制與政策應用。課程將結合理論基礎、實務案例與實際監測資料分析，培養學生理解空氣污染形成機制、監測數據判讀能力，並具備將監測結果應用於污染管制與決策支援之能力。
課程綱要.授課內容: 本課程採授課與實務導向研討並行方式進行，課程內容將涵蓋空氣污染物監測原理、固定站與移動式監測系統、遙測與低成本感測器應用，以及污染管制與法規架構。課程中將透過實際監測資料、案例研究與學生報告，引導學生進行資料分析與污染特性判讀。學生需針對特定空氣污染監測或管制相關主題進行資料分析或專題報告，以培養其實務應用與問題解決能力。

課程綱要.課程名稱(英文): Water Resource Development and Risk Assessment
課程綱要.課程目標: 水是地球上最重要卻具有高度不確定性的資源。本課程旨在培養學生在氣候變遷、人口成長、老舊基礎設施與環境社會需求提升的未來，具備基礎地表與地下水資源知識理論並涉及初步規劃、設計、開發與管理水資源系統的能力。此外，亦包括理解在未來高氣候風險的條件下，如何評估水資源風險的初步概念與理論。 課程將介紹傳統水資源工程（地表/地下水開發、灌溉、供水等）與當國際上常用的風險導向決策方法結合。課程包括理論講授、量化分析、案例與學期中與期末的專題報告，讓學生學會提出「技術可行、經濟合理、環境友善、社會公平、具氣候韌性」的水資源方案。
課程綱要.授課內容:
Course outline:
Week 1: Introduction to Surface Water Resources
Global water challenges and surface water's role in development (e.g., rivers, lakes, reservoirs)
Hydrologic cycle with emphasis on surface processes (precipitation, runoff, evaporation)
Basic water balance and surface water availability assessment
Week 2: Surface Water Hydrology and Data Analysis
Streamflow measurement and gauging
Hydrograph analysis and baseflow separation
Statistical methods for surface water data (frequency analysis, trends)
Week 3: Dams and Reservoirs for Surface Water Storage
Types of dams and design considerations
Reservoir sizing, storage-yield curves, and operation rules
Sedimentation processes and reservoir life estimation
Week 4: Surface Water Supply Systems
Intake structures and conveyance systems
Urban and rural water supply from surface sources
Water treatment basics for surface water quality issues (e.g., turbidity, pathogens)
Week 5: Irrigation and Agricultural Use of Surface Water
Crop water requirements and irrigation scheduling
Surface irrigation methods (flood, furrow, basin)
Efficiency, salinity management, and drainage systems
Week 6: Hydropower and Multi-Purpose Surface Water Projects
Hydropower potential assessment and plant types (run-of-river, storage)
Environmental impacts of surface water development (e.g., flow alteration, habitat disruption)
Case studies: Multi-purpose dams (e.g., Hoover Dam, Three Gorges)
Mid-term Exam (covering Weeks 1-6)
Week 7: Introduction to Groundwater Resources
Aquifer types, properties, and formation
Groundwater flow principles (Darcy's Law, hydraulic conductivity)
Groundwater in the hydrologic cycle and recharge mechanisms
Week 8: Groundwater Exploration and Assessment
Geophysical methods for aquifer mapping
Well drilling and construction techniques
Aquifer testing (pumping tests, slug tests) and data interpretation
Week 9: Groundwater Hydraulics and Modeling
Well hydraulics (Theis, Jacob methods)
Steady-state and transient flow models
Introduction to numerical modeling (e.g., MODFLOW basics)
Week 10: Groundwater Management and Sustainability
Safe yield vs. sustainable yield concepts
Overexploitation issues (land subsidence, saltwater intrusion)
Managed aquifer recharge (MAR) techniques
Week 11: Groundwater Quality and Contamination
Common contaminants and sources
Groundwater treatment and remediation strategies
Monitoring networks and vulnerability assessment
Week 12: Integrated Groundwater Development Projects
Conjunctive use of surface and groundwater
Legal and policy frameworks for groundwater (e.g., permitting, rights)
Case studies: Major aquifers (e.g., Ogallala, Indo-Gangetic)
Mid-term Project Review (groundwater-focused assignment)
Week 13: Introduction to Risk Assessment in Water Resources
Types of risks: Hydrologic, hydraulic, structural, environmental
Probability, uncertainty, and risk vs. reliability concepts
Risk assessment frameworks (qualitative and quantitative)
Week 14: Flood and Drought Risk Assessment
Flood frequency analysis and design floods
Drought indices (SPI, PDSI) and monitoring
Risk mitigation strategies for extremes
Week 15: Climate Change and Infrastructure Risk
Climate impacts on surface and groundwater resources
Vulnerability assessment and adaptation planning
Resilience in water systems design
Week 16: Comprehensive Risk Management and Case Studies
Integrated risk-informed decision making (e.g., cost-benefit with uncertainty)
Dam safety and failure modes analysis
Course review, student presentations on risk assessment projects, and future challenges
Final Exam (emphasis on Weeks 7-16)

課程綱要.課程目標: “教授學生燃燒學所需之基本物理與化學的整合知識，內容涵蓋流體力學、化學熱力與熱傳學以及化學動力學之基礎，並從理論、實驗等方面進行探討。教學方式著重於物理數學模型之建立與其分析方法，以使學生能具備處理工程應用和研究發展有關燃燒問題之基本分析能力。學生於修課後應具備以下基本知識： 1. 燃燒學之三大基礎內涵，諸如流體力學、化學熱力以及化學動力學等。 2. 燃燒學相關重要參數之定義及其應用。 3. 認識一些重要氣態燃料之燃燒反應機制，諸如甲烷、丙烷、氫氣；另也介紹碳氫液態燃料，用於內燃機引擎。 4. 能整合以上知識並運用於燃燒之基礎理論模式的建立、推導與解析，諸如一維之平火 焰、球形火焰與對衝流火焰等層流火焰。 5. 瞭解預混與非預混燃燒之差異，並熟悉貧油與富油條件對燃燒狀態的影響。 6. 知曉火焰之特性，對於預混與非預混之燃燒有初步的認識。 7. 認識燃燒器之設計原則與方法。 8. 認識燃燒之污染物排放問題及其改善方法。“
課程綱要.授課內容:
“0. Introduction:
This book is about combustion science and technology and, as such, covers not only the basic laws and phenomena related to the physics and chemistry of combustion, but also the implications of the fundamental understanding gaining therein to the principles behind the practical combustion phenomena affecting our daily lives.
1. Chemical thermodynamics:
Chemical thermodynamics is concerned with the description of the equilibrium states of reacting multicomponent systems. Compared to single-component systems in which only thermal equilibrium is required, we are now also interested in chemical equilibrium among all of the components.
2. Chemical kinetics:
In this chapter, we first present the phenomenological law describing the general dependence of reaction rates on reactant concentrations and temperature. We then discuss multistep reactions and some approximation techniques used to simplify the representation of these reaction.
3. Oxidation mechanisms of fuels:
In this chapter we discuss the oxidation mechanisms of specific fuel systems involving hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and various hydrocarbons. The formation of pollutions will also be covered. In particular, the reaction pathways leading to fuel consumption, the formation and destruction of intermediate species, and the final product formation are discussed in a qualitative manner.
4. Transport phenomena:
When the molecules in any region of a fluid medium possess an excess of energy, concentration, or momentum, such that gradients of these properties exist in the neighborhood of this region, the system will attempt to restore spatial uniformity by transporting the relevant property in the direction of the deficient region. The transport occurs even in the absence of any bulk motion in this direction.
5. Conservation equations:
The dynamics and thermodynamics of a chemically reacting flow are governed by the conservation laws of mass, momentum, energy, and the concentration of the individual species. In this chapter, we shall first present a derivation of these conservation equations based on control volume considerations, We shall then derive a simplified form of these equations describing only those effects which are of predominant importance in most of the subsonic combustion phenomena to be studied later.
6. Laminar nonpremixed flames:
Either by nature or design, in most combustion systems fuel and oxidizer are initially spatially separated. If the subsequent mixing between them is not sufficiently fast before chemical reaction is initiated, then the mixing and reaction will take place only in thin reaction zones that separate them.
7. Laminar premixed flames:
In this chapter we shall study the simplest, idealized mode propagation, namely the steady propagation of a one-dimensional, planar, adiabatic, wave relative to a stationary, combustible mixture in the doubly infinite domain. We shall call such a wave a standard wave or standard flame.
8. Limit phenomena:
In this chapter we shall study the transition between burning and nonburning states, namely phenomena involving ignition, extinction, flame stabilization and blowoff, and flammability.“

課程綱要.課程名稱(中文): 電化學分析與應用實務
課程綱要.課程目標: 本課程的目標在培養學生對電化學反應原理、量測技術與工程應用的能力，使其能夠將電化學工具有效運用於材料特性分析、反應機制探討以及能源轉換系統的性能評估。課程從基礎理論出發，逐步延伸至循環伏安法、電化學阻抗分析（EIS）與電解器測試等進階方法，並強調儀器操作能力、數據解析能力與實驗設計。學生在修課過程中，將學習如何從電化學數據辨識關鍵反應行為、判斷材料或系統的限制步驟、提出可行的工程優化方向，並能將所學整合至電催化、水電解、電池、腐蝕防護、高分子薄膜等相關領域。藉由理論、案例與實務操作的結合，期望學生能夠逐步形成以電化學方法診斷與解決問題的能力，並將此專業知識延伸至能源材料開發與永續工程的實際情境中。
課程綱要.授課內容:
第 1 週 (2/27) 228連假休假日
第 2 週 (3/6) 電化學在永續能源中的應用
介紹電化學基本概念、電化學技術在能源材料、電解制氫、電池、腐蝕工程中的重要性。
第 3 週(3/13)電化學熱力學基礎：電位、能斯特方程、化學能與電能轉換
理解氧化還原反應、平衡電位與濃度效應。
第 4 週(3/20)電化學動力學：Butler–Volmer、Tafel 行為與電荷轉移機制
探討過電位來源及其對反應速率的影響。
第 5 週(3/27)電極與電解質界面：雙電層、界面電荷、吸附現象
掌握材料表面結構與電化學行為的關聯。
第 6 週(4/3)清明連假
第 7 週(4/10)循環伏安法（CV）理論與實務操作
訊號解析、掃描速率效應、反應機制判斷、實例分析。
第 8 週(4/17)期中考
第 9 週(4/24) 線性掃描伏安法（LSV）與電催化性能評估
HER/OER/ORR 電流密度、過電位、交換電流密度、近表面反應機制。
第 10 週(5/1)電化學阻抗頻譜（EIS）解析（上）：原理、奈奎斯特圖、波特圖
理解阻抗來源與元件意義。
第 11 週(5/8)EIS 解析（下）：等效電路建模、電荷轉移、傳輸、膜阻抗分析
探討如何從阻抗判讀材料劣化與反應瓶頸。
第 12 週(5/15)半導體電化學、Mott–Schottky 分析與光電化學測試基礎
適用於光催化、光電極水分解材料。
第 13 週(5/22)電解槽與電極系統分析：鹼性電解、PEM、海水電解特性
探討能量效率、電壓損失、離子傳輸與材料限制。
第 14週(5/29)電池電化學分析：鋰電池、鋅電池、燃料電池之性能評估方法
包括充放電曲線、倍率性能、阻抗劣化。
第 15 週(6/5) 腐蝕電化學分析：Tafel 外推法、極化曲線、腐蝕速率量測
實務導向，用於金屬表面工程與防鏽研究。
第 16 (6/12) 週 期末考

課程綱要.課程名稱(英文): Enabling the Transition: Hydrogen and Carbon Management Technologies Across Key Sectors
課程綱要.課程目標: This course aims to explore in depth the complementary roles that two major technological pathways—hydrogen technologies and carbon dioxide (CO₂) capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS)—can play in accelerating the energy transition and decarbonizing energy systems at the territorial scale. Hydrogen is a zero-carbon energy carrier that can serve multiple purposes: it can be used directly for electricity or heat generation, act as a means to store and transport energy, and serve as a feedstock for the production of value-added products such as synthetic fuels and chemicals. It also has the ability to couple energy networks (electricity, gas, heat), facilitating greater system integration and flexibility. In parallel, CO₂ capture followed by storage or utilization aims to mitigate emissions from hard-to-abate sectors such as heavy industry (e.g. cement, steel) and fossil-based energy production. When applied to emissions from biomass resources or direct air capture, CO2 storage or utilization even contribute to negative emissions. The course will begin with a broad overview of the energy transition, its implications for energy system design and the emerging roles of hydrogen technologies and CO2 capture, utilization and storage. We will then dive into the technical fundamentals of hydrogen and CCUS value chains. Throughout the course, we will examine deployment challenges and opportunities, including existing national roadmaps, real-world projects, regulatory frameworks, financing mechanisms, and societal dimensions such as social acceptability and stakeholder engagement. The course includes group work focusing on how these technologies might contribute to Taiwan’s GHG emissions reduction and its net-zero target, culminating in student presentations and a collective discussion of key takeaways and recommendations.
課程綱要.授課內容:
1. Energy Transition and the Evolution of Energy Systems
Overview of global and national decarbonization goals, transition scenarios, and the emerging roles of hydrogen and CCUS within future energy systems.
2. Hydrogen Technologies: Value Chains and Key Components
In-depth exploration of hydrogen production methods (electrolysis, SMR, etc.), storage, transportation, and end-uses across various sectors.
3. CO₂ Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS): Value Chains and Technologies
Detailed analysis of CO₂ sources, capture technologies (post-combustion, pre-combustion, oxyfuel), transportation options, storage solutions, and utilization pathways.
4. Group Work Briefing: Assessing the Potential for Hydrogen and CCUS in Taiwan
Introduction to group assignment. Presentation of the Taiwanese context: energy mix, decarbonization strategy, challenges, and opportunities for deploying hydrogen and CCUS.
5. Hydrogen Deployment: National Roadmaps, Projects, and Barriers
Review of existing hydrogen strategies and flagship projects worldwide. Discussion of regulatory, technical, and financial enablers and barriers to deployment.
6. CCUS Deployment: Strategies, Projects, and Implementation Challenges
Analysis of real-world CCUS projects, national roadmaps, and the specific challenges related to infrastructure, regulation, and public support.
7. Societal Dimensions: Public Acceptance and Stakeholder Engagement
Examination of public perception, risk communication, and best practices for building trust and acceptance of hydrogen and CCUS technologies.
8. Group Presentations: Hydrogen and CCUS Pathways for Taiwan
Student-led presentations analyzing the feasibility, benefits, and risks of implementing hydrogen and/or CCUS technologies in Taiwan.
9. Conclusion and Outlook: Will These Technologies Deliver?
Synthesis of lessons learned throughout the course. Critical assessment of hydrogen and CCUS contributions to net-zero targets. Final recommendations.
